name: Wewak
note: Town: provincial capital of East Sepik and the gateway for Sepik River trips and the Wewak islands; WWII Japanese airbase and surrender site.

name: Vanimo
note: Town: capital of Sandaun Province on the Indonesian border; base for the surf breaks and the coastal headlands.

name: Aitape
note: Town: north-coast mission town between Wewak and Vanimo, hit by the 1998 Sissano tsunami; named by Wikivoyage Sepik as a town, no visitor sights listed.

name: Maprik
note: Town and district: the Maprik area holds the best-known haus tambaran spirit houses; Wikipedia article is the district.

name: Angoram
note: River town: station town on the lower Sepik, one of three river villages reached by road from Wewak (Wikivoyage Sepik).

name: Ambunti
note: River town: middle Sepik town and host of the Sepik River Crocodile and Arts Festival (PTPA Momase).

name: Pagwi
note: River village: Sepik village reached by road from Wewak, near the Chambri Lakes, with basic guesthouses and a carved council house.

name: Timbunke
note: River village: Sepik village reached by road from Wewak; site of the July 1945 Japanese massacre of villagers (Wikipedia Sepik River).

name: Telefomin
note: Remote station town in the Sandaun interior, reached by air; Baptist Mission museum and fossils (Wikipedia). Wikivoyage Sepik names it only as one of the most remote towns.

name: Sepik River
coordinates_source: osm:node/2643833870 Angoram (river visitor access point, not the river centroid); Wikipedia article Sepik
note: River: the Sepik, PNG's longest river, visited by motor-canoe and riverboat trips to river villages; a long linear feature, pin at its main visitor access (Wewak, Angoram, Pagwi). Pinned at Angoram, a river-town access point, not the river centroid.

name: Chambri Lakes
coordinates_source: osm:relation/7573782 natural=water centroid (lake; Chambri Lakes in water is correct)
note: Lake system: seasonal lakes and canals in the middle Sepik near Pagwi, home to the Chambri villages; a river-trip stop per tour material (no counted visitor listing found).

name: Murik Lakes
coordinates_source: osm:node/13786457027 natural=bay centroid (no visitor point in OSM)
note: Lake and lagoon system at the Sepik mouth with Murik villages (Mendam, Karau); named as a river-trip stop in tour material found by web search, no counted visitor page or Wikipedia article.

name: Sissano Lagoon
note: Lagoon: formed by the 1908 tsunami and devastated by the 1998 Aitape tsunami (about 2,000 dead); Wikivoyage Sepik names it near Aitape, no visitor facilities listed.

name: Kairiru Island
note: Island: volcanic island 30 minutes by boat off Wewak with waterfalls, snorkelling and natural hot springs (PTPA); guesthouse per Wikivoyage. Wikipedia title 'Kairiru' is the language.

name: Mushu Island
note: Island: coral atoll with a white-sand beach and reef fish, half an hour off Wewak; basic guesthouse. Named Muschu by PTPA. Wikipedia title is the Disney character.

name: Robuin Island
note: Island: uninhabited island off Wewak owned by Wom village, Japanese fuel dump bombed in WWII; named in Wikivoyage Sepik and Remote Lands.

name: Wuvulu Island
note: Island: remote flat coral island of the Western Admiralty group, ringed by reef, named by Wikivoyage Sepik for diving. Administratively Manus Province, outside this region's two provinces; route to the islands region.

name: Cape Wom
coordinates_source: osm:node/11799415670 monument (Cape Wom Memorial); agrees with Wikipedia within 100 m
note: WWII memorial: peace park where General Adachi signed the Japanese surrender in New Guinea in 1945, with open Japanese tunnels; PTPA calls it the Wom Memorial and Japanese Peace Park.

name: Wom Beach
note: Beach: palm-fringed beach near Cape Wom, named by PTPA Momase as a main attraction in and near Wewak; may be the same stop as Cape Wom.

name: Mission Hill
note: Hill: lookout hill in Wewak named by PTPA Momase as a main attraction; no further description in sources found.

name: Grand Chief Sir Michael Somare Memorial
coordinates_source: osm:way/141772375 Somare Park (way centre; memorial site inferred, MEDIUM-LOW)
note: Memorial: monument in Wewak to Michael Somare, PNG's first prime minister, named by PTPA Momase as a main attraction; a minor memorial unless visitors do more than stop.

name: Vanimo Surf Breaks
coordinates_source: osm:node/1250713739 natural=cape Vanimo Point (area point; surf breaks not named in any source)
note: Surf breaks: consistent reef and point breaks west of Vanimo, up to 3 m, best September to March (Wikivoyage); experienced surfers only.

name: Vanimo Headlands
note: Coastal headlands: limestone peninsula near Vanimo with tribal villages, beaches and snorkelling (Remote Lands); a headland area rather than a named site.

name: Japanese Barge Wreck, Vanimo
note: WWII wreck: rusting Japanese barge from the occupation, near the Vanimo headlands (Remote Lands); no name or position in any source.

name: Maprik Haus Tambaran
coordinates_source: osm:node/1363471946 place=town Maprik (area point; no single haus tambaran sited)
note: Spirit houses: haus tambaran ancestral worship houses, with the best examples around Maprik, painted and carved (Wikivoyage Sepik); visited through village tours.

name: Palimbei
note: Village: thatched Sepik village with a carved and painted Haus Tambaran and sago cooking demonstration (Remote Lands); spelled Palimbi or Palambe elsewhere.

name: Mindimbit
note: Village: large Iatmul village on the middle Sepik known for moon-faced carved figures and wooden masks (Remote Lands).

name: Kanganaman
note: Village: small East Sepik village with a basic village guesthouse (Remote Lands); lodging, not a sight.

name: Torricelli Mountains
note: Mountain range: Sandaun range with Mount Sulen (1,657 m) and tree-kangaroo habitat; Wikipedia only, no visitor source names it as a place to go.

name: Bewani Mountains
note: Mountain range: highest point 1,960 m in northwest Sandaun, a biodiversity range; Wikipedia only, no visitor source names it as a place to go.

name: Prince Alexander Mountains
note: Mountain range: range on the north coast with Mount Turu, home of the Abelam yam-growing people; Wikipedia only, no visitor source names it as a place to go.

name: Sepik Crocodile and Arts Festival
note: Festival: annual Sepik crocodile and arts festival held in Ambunti (PTPA) with village performances; an event, not a permanent place.

name: Sepik Bilum and Basket Show
note: Festival: annual three-day bilum and basket show in Wewak (October 2026 edition on PTPA's homepage); an event, not a permanent place.
